title: Temple, Exile and Return
objective: After this level you can explain how the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple in 586 BCE and again in 70 CE reshaped Jewish life.
summary: Babylon destroyed the First Temple in 586 BCE; exiles kept faith through the Sabbath and prayer. The rebuilt Temple fell to Rome in 70 CE; the Western Wall and Tisha b'Av keep its memory.

cards.headline: Twice, the center of Jewish worship was destroyed.
cards.body: The Temple in Jerusalem became the only place of sacrifice in Judah. It was lost in 586 BCE, rebuilt, and lost again in 70 CE. Each loss changed how Jews lived their faith.

cards.headline: The First Temple falls
cards.body: The First Temple was completed under King Solomon in the 10th century BCE, and in time it became the only place of sacrifice in Judah. Then, in 586 BCE, the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II destroyed Jerusalem and its Temple, and many Judeans were deported to Babylonia. Imagine your whole religious life built around one building, and then the building is gone.

cards.headline: Faith by the rivers of Babylon
cards.body: In exile, Jews kept the Sabbath and holy days, practiced circumcision and offered prayers in place of the Temple's sacrifices. Some scholars think synagogues began then. A psalm keeps the grief: "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion." Without knowing it, the exiles were practicing Judaism without a Temple.

cards.headline: Return, and a second loss
cards.body: In 538 BCE Cyrus the Great, the Persian king who had conquered Babylonia, let the Jews go home, though some chose to stay. The rebuilt Temple was completed in 515 BCE. It stood for centuries, until the Romans destroyed it in 70 CE, during a Jewish rebellion against Rome.

cards.headline: What remains
cards.body: The Western Wall is a surviving stretch of the wall that ringed the Temple Mount. It is a place of prayer, where people push slips of paper with prayers into the cracks. Each July or August, on the fast of Tisha b'Av, many Jews mourn both Temples and read the Book of Lamentations.

cards.headline: Temple, Exile and Return: the takeaways
learned: Babylon destroyed the First Temple in 586 BCE and exiled many Jews
In exile, prayer took the place of sacrifice
Rome destroyed the Second Temple in 70 CE; Tisha b'Av mourns both

questions.prompt: Put these in order of their part in the Temple's story, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: The First Temple was completed under King Solomon, destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar II in 586 BCE; Cyrus the Great let the Jews go home in 538 BCE; the Romans destroyed the rebuilt Temple in 70 CE.

questions.prompt: What is the Western Wall in Jerusalem?

options.label: A surviving part of the wall that ringed the Temple Mount
The front wall of the First Temple itself
options.rationale: It belonged to the retaining wall around the Mount.

options.label: A wall built after 1900 as a memorial
Part of Babylon's walls, brought back by exiles
options.rationale: It stands where it was built, in Jerusalem.

questions.explanation: The Western Wall is a surviving part of the retaining wall around the Temple Mount.

questions.prompt: In Babylon, exiles offered prayers in place of sacrifices. Why would that matter again after 70 CE?

options.label: Because Cyrus had banned all sacrifices
options.rationale: Cyrus let the exiles rebuild the Temple.

options.label: Because the Temple was gone again, so worship had to go on without it
Because the Romans rebuilt the Temple in Babylon
Because prayer was only allowed at the Western Wall

questions.explanation: After Rome destroyed the Second Temple, Jews again had to worship without sacrifice, as the exiles had.
